extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent applicants, and patent practitioners (petitioners/protestors)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluative standards in MPEP for handling petitions alleging public use/on-sale bars and for submission, treatment, and possible expungement of trade secret/proprietary/protective-order materials during patent prosecution, reissue, and reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of petition for consideration prior to first Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition should be filed early if petitioner wishes it considered prior to the first Office action on the application. Petitioners should be aware that the Office will entertain petitions under 37 CFR 1.183, when accompanied by the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(h), to waive the 2-month delay period of 37 CFR 1.176 in appropriate circumstances. Accordingly, petitioners in reissue applications cannot automatically assume that the full 2-month delay period of 37 CFR 1.176 will always be available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File petitions early; consider filing a 1.183 petition with fee to waive delay when appropriate; do not assume automatic availability of the 2-month delay for reissue applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification search when application number unknown
rubrics_metrics.description: In ex parte situations where a petitioner cannot identify the pending application by application number, the petition papers will be forwarded to the appropriate TC Director for an identification search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petition lacks application number, Office forwards papers to TC Director to locate the file; once located, forward to OPLA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and duplicate-filing requirements for petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petition filed in the Office does not indicate service on applicant or applicant’s attorney or agent, and is not filed in duplicate, then the Office will undertake to determine whether or not service has been made by contacting applicant or applicant’s attorney or agent. If service has not been made and no duplicate has been filed, then the Office may request petitioner to file such a duplicate before the petition is referred to the examiner. Alternatively, if the petition involves only a few pages, the Office may, in its sole discretion, elect to reproduce the petition rather than delay referring it to the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always indicate service and file duplicate where required; the Office may contact parties to determine service and may request duplicates or reproduce short petitions; note when Office mails duplicate to applicant that the file should reflect it by transmittal letter or notation in Contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling untimely petitions after notice of allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petition is not submitted prior to the mailing of a notice of allowance under 37 CFR 1.311, it should not be entered in the application file. The applicant should be notified that the petition is untimely and that it is not being entered in the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If untimely, notify applicant and do not enter petition; specific handling varies: (A) if service of copy included, original petition should be discarded; (B) where service not included, duplicate copy (if present) discarded and original sent to applicant with notification of nonentry.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPLA screening under 37 CFR 1.292 and referral to examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the Office of Patent Legal Administration (OPLA) staff member has determined that the petition meets the formal requirements of 37 CFR 1.292, and the application’s status warrants consideration of the petition, he or she will prepare a letter for the Patent Legal Administrator, forwarding the petition and the application file to the examiner for determination of whether a prima facie case of public use or sale in this country of the claimed subject matter is established by the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPLA determines formal sufficiency and whether application status warrants evaluation; then forwards petition, any party papers, and the file to the examiner for prima facie determination; acceptance of additional papers is discretionary but protracted filings discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prima facie showing standard for public use/on-sale bar
rubrics_metrics.description: A prima facie case is established by the petition if the examiner finds that the facts asserted in the affidavit(s) or declaration(s), as supported by the exhibits, if later proved true by testimony taken in the public use proceeding, would result in a statutory bar to the claims under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) alone or in combination with 35 U.S.C. 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must identify exactly what was in public use or on sale, whether it was in use/on sale in this country more than 1 year before the effective filing date, and whether the pending claims read on or are obvious over the alleged public use/on-sale matter; compare all pending claims with the alleged matter, not just claims identified by petitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint content when petition alleges obviousness over public use/on-sale matter
rubrics_metrics.description: In situations where the petition alleges only that the claims are obvious over subject matter asserted to be in public use or on sale, the petition should include prior art or other information on which it relies and explain how the prior art or other information in combination with the subject matter asserted to be in public use or on sale renders the claims obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner should supply the supporting prior art or rationale and explain combinations; examiner is not expected to perform a prior art search in evaluating the petition, but may rely on known prior art to find a prima facie case of obviousness even if petition alleged only anticipation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner memorandum to Patent Legal Administrator
rubrics_metrics.description: After having made his/her determination, the examiner will forward a memorandum to the Patent Legal Administrator, stating his or her findings and his or her decision as to whether a prima facie case has been established. The findings should include a summary of the alleged facts, a comparison of at least one claim with the device alleged to be in public use or on sale, and any other pertinent facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare memorandum in triplicate, addressed to Patent Legal Administrator, and include sufficient factual summary and claim-to-device comparison to aid the preliminary hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary hearing procedures and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner concludes that a prima facie showing has been established, the Commissioner may hold a preliminary hearing. The notification of this hearing amounts to an order to show cause why a public use proceeding should not be held. No new evidence is to be introduced or discussed at this hearing. The format of the hearing is established by OPLA staff and the Patent Legal Administrator presides; the examiner may attend as an observer only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In ex parte hearings, avoid discussion of application matters not already known to petitioner; examiner’s memorandum is not forwarded to the petitioner in ex parte cases; applicant may notify petitioner of claim nature by action or consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public use proceeding evidence rule (testimony requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory bar can only be established by testimony taken in accordance with normal rules of evidence, including the right of cross-examination. The affidavits or declarations are not to be considered part of the testimony and in no case can they be used as evidence on behalf of the party submitting them unless submitted as part of that party’s testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits/declarations supporting the petition establish only prima facie case; live testimony with opportunity for cross-examination is required to conclusively establish the statutory bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule for testimony, records, and briefs in public use proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner will set a schedule of times for taking testimony and for filing the record and briefs on the basis of the following template: (A) testimony for petitioner to close ~60 days after letter; (B) applicant objections to close ~20 days after (A); (C) petitioner supplemental evidence to close 20 days after (B); (D) applicant to request cross-examination to close ~20 days after (C); (E) cross-examination to close ~30 days after (D); (F) rebuttal testimony by applicant to close ~20 days after (E). Filing schedule for record and briefs follows with approximate intervals; no extension under 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific dates to avoid confusion; parties may agree different schedule provided last brief is no later than the date set; certified deposition transcripts must be filed within one month after deposition; all papers served per 37 CFR 1.248.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on testimony topics in public use proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In all public use proceedings, whether the ultimate issue is anticipation under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) or obviousness over 35 U.S.C. 103, testimony will be limited to the issues of public use or on sale. No testimony will be received on whether the claimed subject matter would have been obvious over subject matter asserted to be in public use or on sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testimony focuses on factual issues of public use/on-sale; questions of legal obviousness over prior art are not to be explored by testimony in these proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final decision preparation and content (examiner)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final decision of the examiner should be 'analogous [to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences] in an interference proceeding, analyzing the testimony' and stating conclusions. The examiner is not bound by the prior finding that a prima facie case has been established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a public use or sale bar is found, enter a rejection predicated on the evidence and the findings; if not, the written action should indicate that the evidence of 35 U.S.C. 102(b) activity was considered; strictly adhere to format so rationale is self-evident; consider reasons for allowance per 37 CFR 1.104(e) where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of review of examiner’s final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no review from the final decision of the examiner in the public use proceedings. A petition under 37 CFR 1.181 requesting the Commissioner exercise supervisory authority to vacate the examiner’s decision will not be entertained except where there is a showing of clear error. Once the application returns to its ex parte status, appellate review under 35 U.S.C. 134 and 141-145 may be had of any adverse decision rejecting claim(s) as a result of the examiner’s decisions as to public use or sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition under 1.181 is limited to clear error; standard appellate avenues apply after return to ex parte status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose trade secret/proprietary/protective-order materials (37 CFR 1.56/1.555)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventors and others covered by 37 CFR 1.56(c) and 1.555 have a duty to disclose to the Office information they are aware of which is material to patentability. 37 CFR 1.56(b) states that information is material to patentability when it is not cumulative and (1) it establishes, by itself or in combination, a prima facie case of unpatentability of a claim; or (2) it refutes, or is inconsistent with, a position the applicant takes in opposing an argument of unpatentability relied on by the Office, or asserting an argument of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade secret or proprietary classification does not relieve the duty to disclose material information; applicants/patent owners must disclose material information even if subject to protective order; a prima facie case uses preponderance standard and broadest reasonable claim construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible redaction/deletion when submitting trade secret material
rubrics_metrics.description: In some circumstances it may be possible to submit the information in such a manner that legitimate trade secrets, etc., will not be disclosed, e.g., by appropriate deletions of nonmaterial portions of the information. This should be done only where there will be no loss of information material to patentability under 37 CFR 1.56 or 1.555.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redact only nonmaterial portions and ensure no loss of material information; do not submit favorable-to-patentability information under MPEP § 724.02 (e.g., commercial success) as such information is not to be handled under this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of submitting trade secret/proprietary/protective-order materials (labeling and packaging)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information considered trade secret/proprietary or subject to a protective order must be clearly labeled as such and be filed in a sealed, clearly labeled, envelope or container. Each document or item must be clearly labeled as a 'Trade Secret' document or item, a 'Proprietary' document or item, or as an item or document 'Subject To Protective Order.' It is essential that the terms 'Confidential,' 'Restricted' or 'Restricted Data' not be used when marking these documents or items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Envelopes/containers and each document must bear complete identifying information (application, application no., title, TC art unit, examiner, attention/location); transmittal letter with same identifying information is required and should state materials are submitted under MPEP § 724; petition to expunge may accompany submission; hand-carry preferred, but mailing allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate envelope labels (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of appropriate labels for such an envelope or container addressed to an application are given (e.g., 'TRADE SECRET MATERIAL NOT OPEN TO PUBLIC. TO BE OPENED ONLY BY EXAMINER OR OTHER AUTHORIZED U.S. PATENT AND TRADEMARK OFFICE EMPLOYEE. In re Application of ... Application No. ... Filed: ... For: (Title of Invention) TC Art Unit: Examiner: ATTENTION: (Current Location of Application)') and analogous labels for 'PROPRIETARY MATERIAL' and 'MATERIAL SUBJECT TO PROTECTIVE ORDER'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provided wording templates and include tribunal/identification data when 'subject to protective order.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of material appropriate for submission under MPEP § 724.02
rubrics_metrics.description: The types of materials or information contemplated for submission under MPEP § 724.02 include information 'material to patentability' but does not include information favorable to patentability. Thus, any trade secret, proprietary, and/or protective order materials which are required to be submitted on behalf of a patent applicant under 37 CFR 1.56 or patent owner under 37 CFR 1.555 can be submitted in accordance with MPEP § 724.02. Neither 37 CFR 1.56 nor 1.555 require disclosure of information favorable to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit evidence of commercial success or other favorable evidence under §724.02; if such materials appear in amendments/arguments/affidavits under specified regs they will be of record and not given special status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protestor submissions and limitations pre- and post-publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions can be made in accordance with MPEP § 724.02 before the patent application is published, if protestor or petitioner has access to the application. After the patent application has been published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b)(1), no protest may be filed without the express consent of the applicant. Any submission filed by a protestor must follow requirements for service. The Office cannot ensure that the party or parties served will maintain the information secret.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If protestor must comment on submitted material without revealing details, either (A) avoid disclosing details or (B) submit comments in separate paper under MPEP § 724.02; follow service rules; obtain applicant consent post-publication before protesting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office handling of submitted materials pending determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt, the transmittal letter and the envelope or container will be date stamped and brought to the attention of the examiner or other Office employee responsible for evaluating the submission. The receipt will be noted on the 'Contents' of the file. The face of the application or reexamination file will have a notation placed thereon to indicate that trade secret, proprietary, or protective order material has been filed. The location of the material will also be specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office personnel must not disclose such materials to the public without authorization; maintain clear notations on file wrapper indicating presence and location of materials (e.g., words 'TRADE SECRET MATERIALS FILED WHICH ARE NOT OPEN TO PUBLIC').

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when submitted materials are in applications covered by 35 U.S.C. 122
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted material will be maintained in the original envelope or container (clearly marked 'Not Open To The Public') and will not be publicly available until a determination has been made as to whether or not the information is important to a reasonable examiner. After publication under 35 U.S.C. 122(b)(1), copies of submitted material should not be made available to any member of the public requesting a copy of the pending application file wrapper under 37 CFR 1.14(c)(2) so long as the application is pending. If the published application is abandoned and a petition to expunge was not filed, the material will be available to the public under 37 CFR 1.14(c) or (e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner/appropriate official will decide whether information is important to a reasonable examiner; if important, cite in next Office action and make part of file history; if not important, indicate this in next Office action without details and reseal the information pending petition to expunge; mark 'Not Open To The Public' while petition pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment in reissue and reexamination files open to the public
rubrics_metrics.description: For materials submitted in reissue applications open to the public under 37 CFR 1.11(b) and reexamination files open under 37 CFR 1.11(d): submitted information will be maintained separate from the file and not publicly available until a determination as to importance to a reasonable examiner is made; if found important it will be cited in the next Office action and become part of the file and open to the public; if not important, reseal and retain separate pending petition to expunge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handling is similar to original applications but emphasizes keeping submitted material separate from public file until determination; pending petitions should have sealed container marked 'Not Open To The Public.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to expunge requirements (37 CFR 1.59(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.59(b) to expunge information submitted under MPEP § 724.02 will be entertained only if the petition fee (37 CFR 1.17(h)) is filed and the information has been found not to be important to a reasonable examiner in deciding on patentability. If the information is found to be important to a reasonable examiner, any petition to expunge will be denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition to expunge should accompany submission and be filed early so it can be acted on before patent issues or application is abandoned; petitions must be directed to the Technology Center and include: (A) clear identification of information to be expunged without disclosure of details; (B) statement that information is trade secret/proprietary/or subject to protective order and not otherwise public; (C) commitment to retain information for period of any patent; (D) statement that petition submitted by party in interest who originally submitted the information; (E) the required fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)). Timing is critical — if decision not made before issue or abandonment, material will remain and be open to public.
